s: The policy repo rate is regarded as the main monetary-policy instrument because the Monetary Policy Committee sets it primarily to
o: achieve the inflation target and guide money-market rates
determine the annual SLR ceiling of 40 per cent
fix the exchange rate of the Indian rupee permanently
x: The MPC sets the policy repo rate to achieve the inflation target, while liquidity operations help keep money-market rates close to that rate.

s: Which one of the following is the primary objective of monetary policy under the flexible inflation-targeting framework?
o: Maintaining price stability while keeping growth in mind
x: Price stability is the primary objective, with growth kept in mind. Financial stability is also a recognised objective, whereas the other functions listed are not primary monetary-policy objectives.

s: Under inflation targeting, what does the central bank publicly announce?
x: Inflation targeting means publicly announcing a medium-term numerical target for inflation.

s:
Consider the following statements about the flexible inflation-targeting framework:
1. The Central Government sets the inflation target.
2. The RBI conducts monetary policy to achieve the target.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement divides the work: the Government sets the target and the RBI conducts monetary policy to achieve it.

s: Under Section 45ZN of the RBI Act, at what level must average CPI inflation remain for failure to meet the inflation target to be deemed?
o: above 4 per cent or below 2 per cent for four consecutive quarters
above 6 per cent or below 2 per cent for three consecutive quarters
above 6 per cent or below 2 per cent for three consecutive months
above 5 per cent or below 3 per cent for two consecutive quarters
x: Failure is defined as average CPI inflation remaining above 6 per cent or below 2 per cent for three consecutive quarters. The statutory wording refers to quarters, not months.

s: When the inflation target is missed in the statutory manner, what is the Reserve Bank of India required to report to the Government?
o: exchange-rate level it will maintain for the next financial year
reasons for failure, remedial actions and estimated time to return to the target
names of all MPC members and their individual salaries
future Union Budget allocations and tax rates
x: The RBI must report the reasons for the failure, the remedial actions proposed and the period within which inflation is expected to return to the target.

s: How often does the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, set the inflation target?
x: Under Section 45ZA the Centre, with the RBI, sets the target once every five years and notifies it in the Official Gazette.

s: Where is the inflation target set by the Centre under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act notified?
x: The target, set once every five years by the Centre with the RBI, is notified in the Official Gazette.

s: What was the inflation target notified for the period from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031?
o: 5 per cent with a tolerance band of 2 percentage points
4 per cent with a tolerance band of 2 percentage points
2 per cent with a tolerance band of 1 percentage point
6 per cent with a tolerance band of 1 percentage point
x: The 25 March 2026 notification retained the 4 per cent CPI target with a 2 percentage point tolerance band for 2026–2031.

s: Which inflation-target notification – period covered pair is correctly matched?
x: The 25 March 2026 notification covers April 2026–March 2031; the August 2016 one covered up to March 2021 and the March 2021 one April 2021–March 2026.

s: What is the base year of the new CPI-Combined series released by the NSO (MoSPI) in February 2026?
x: CPI-Combined, the nominal anchor for the inflation target, is compiled by the NSO under MoSPI; the new series of 12 February 2026 has base year 2024 (earlier 2012).

s: When was the 4 per cent inflation target first notified?
x: The target was first notified in August 2016 for the period to 31 March 2021.

s: Who compiles the CPI-Combined, the anchor of the inflation target?
x: Headline CPI-C is compiled by the NSO under MoSPI.

s: The new CPI series released in February 2026 (base 2024) replaced the series with which base year?
x: The new CPI-C series has base 2024; the earlier base was 2012.

s: In which year was the failure clause under India's flexible inflation-targeting framework first invoked?
x: The failure clause was first invoked in 2022; March 2026 marked the second retention of the original target.

s: Which committee recommended monetary targeting with feedback and was associated with the organised money market in India?
x: The Sukhamoy Chakravarty Committee, constituted in 1985, recommended monetary targeting with feedback and dealt with the organised money market.

s: The blueprint for the money market that subsequently led to the introduction of Commercial Paper in 1990 was associated with which committee?
x: N. Vaghul headed the 1987 committee that prepared a blueprint for the money market and contributed to the introduction of Commercial Paper in 1990.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Urjit Patel Committee’s recommendations?
o: Creation of a committee to decide policy rates
Adoption of CPI as the nominal anchor
A 4 per cent inflation target with a tolerance band of 2 percentage points
Continuation of the multiple-indicator approach as the sole framework
x: The Urjit Patel Committee recommended dropping the multiple-indicator approach, adopting CPI as the nominal anchor and establishing an MPC-based rate-setting framework.

s: With which subject did the S. S. Tarapore Committee of 1997 deal?
x: Tarapore (1997; second in 2006) dealt with capital account convertibility.

s: In which year did the Urjit Patel Committee recommend flexible inflation targeting?
x: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended FIT with 4% ±2% CPI.

s: The Urjit Patel Committee recommended which index as the nominal anchor of monetary policy?
x: It recommended CPI-C as the nominal anchor; the anchor is CPI-C, not WPI.

s:
Arrange the following committees on monetary policy in chronological order:
1. Urjit Patel Committee
2. Vaghul Committee
3. Sukhamoy Chakravarty Committee
4. Tarapore Committee
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Chakravarty 1985, Vaghul 1987, Tarapore 1997 and Urjit Patel 2014.

s: In which year did the Sukhamoy Chakravarty Committee on the working of the monetary system recommend monetary targeting?
x: The Chakravarty Committee (1985) recommended monetary targeting with feedback, using M3.

s: The RBI (Amendment) Act, 2016 inserted which range of sections into the RBI Act, 1934 in connection with the monetary policy framework?
x: The 2016 amendment inserted Sections 45Z to 45ZO into the RBI Act, 1934, providing the statutory framework for the MPC and inflation-targeting provisions.

s: The inflation target is set by the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, under which section of the RBI Act, 1934?
x: Section 45ZA covers the inflation target (set every five years and notified in the Gazette); Section 45ZB constitutes the MPC.

s: The Monetary Policy Committee is constituted under which provision of the RBI Act, 1934?
x: Section 45ZB provides for the constitution of the Monetary Policy Committee. Section 45ZA concerns the inflation target, while Section 45ZN deals with failure to meet the target.

s: On which date was the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement between the Government and the RBI signed?
x: The MPFA was signed on 20 Feb 2015; the RBI (Amendment) Act came in May 2016.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement?
o: It was signed by the Government and the RBI
It formally adopted flexible inflation targeting
It is a statute enacted by Parliament
The RBI is answerable for missing the target
x: The MPFA (2015) is an agreement, not a statute; the statute is the RBI (Amendment) Act, 2016.

s: Which Act inserted Sections 45Z to 45ZO into the RBI Act, giving statutory backing to the MPC?
x: The RBI (Amendment) Act, 2016 (May 2016) inserted Sections 45Z to 45ZO, giving statutory basis to flexible inflation targeting and the MPC.

s: Under the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement of 2015, below what level was CPI inflation to be brought by January 2016?
x: The MPFA aimed to bring CPI inflation below 6% by January 2016.

s: Who headed the committee associated with inflation targeting at 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%?
x: The Urjit Patel committee is linked with 4% ± 2% inflation targeting; Nachiket Mor is associated with financial inclusion and Shanta Kumar with FCI/PDS reform.

s: What is the status of the decisions of the Monetary Policy Committee?
o: Advisory and not binding on the RBI
Subject to approval by the RBI Central Board
x: MPC decisions are binding on the RBI; the inflation target itself is set by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the composition of the Monetary Policy Committee?
o: The RBI Governor is its Chairperson ex officio
The three external members are appointed by the RBI Central Board
The Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy is an ex officio member
One RBI officer is nominated by the RBI Central Board
x: The three external members are appointed by the Central Government (for four years), not by the RBI Central Board.

s: For what term are the external members of the Monetary Policy Committee appointed?
o: Four years and are not eligible for reappointment
Two years and are eligible for unlimited reappointment
Five years and are appointed by the RBI Central Board
Three years and are eligible for one reappointment
x: The three external members are appointed by the Central Government for four years and are not eligible for reappointment.

s: By law, at least how many times a year must the Monetary Policy Committee meet?
x: The law requires at least four meetings a year; meeting six times (bi-monthly) is only the practice.

s: What is the quorum for a meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee?
x: Quorum is 4, including the Governor or, in his absence, the Deputy Governor.

s: In case of a tie in the Monetary Policy Committee, what does the RBI Governor have?
x: The Governor chairs the MPC and has a casting vote on a tie, not a veto.

s: By whom is the one RBI officer on the Monetary Policy Committee nominated?
x: The RBI officer is nominated by the RBI Central Board; external members are appointed by the Central Government.

s: When did the Monetary Policy Committee hold its first meeting?
x: The MPC first met in October 2016.

s: How many external members are there in the six-member Monetary Policy Committee?
x: The MPC has 3 RBI members and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government.

s: Who traced the phases of India's monetary-policy evolution in the lecture titled “Seven Ages of India's Monetary Policy”?
x: Governor Shaktikanta Das traced these phases in “Seven Ages of India's Monetary Policy” on 24 January 2020 at St. Stephen's College.

s: Which approach to monetary policy prevailed in India during 1998–2014?
x: Monetary targeting (1985–1998) was followed by the multiple-indicator approach (1998–2014), the glide path (2014–2016) and FIT from 2016.

s: The multiple-indicator approach (1998–2014) was criticised for being:
x: The multiple-indicator approach was criticised as opaque.

s: In which year did Shaktikanta Das deliver the 'Seven Ages of India's Monetary Policy' speech?
x: Shaktikanta Das delivered the speech on 24 January 2020.

s: Between May 2022 and February 2023, over what range was the policy repo rate raised?
x: The repo rate was increased from 4 per cent to 6.5 per cent during May 2022–February 2023, reflecting a tightening phase.

s: In April 2025, when the repo rate was cut to 6 per cent, to which stance did the RBI's monetary policy move from neutral?
x: The stance moved from neutral to accommodative in April 2025 with the cut to 6 per cent; it was neutral in 2026 when the repo rate was held at 5.25 per cent.

s: What does the policy stance 'withdrawal of accommodation' signal?
o: a tightening bias that drains excess liquidity
x: Withdrawal of accommodation is a tightening bias that drains excess liquidity.

s: In December 2025, to what level was the policy repo rate cut by 25 bps?
x: In Dec 2025 the repo was cut 25 bps to 5.25% and held there through Aug 2026.

s: Critics of flexible inflation targeting in India argue that the headline inflation target should be replaced by which measure?
x: Critics argue for a core-inflation target because food and supply shocks, which drive headline inflation, are outside the MPC's direct control.

s: Global monetary tightening can affect India through capital outflows, pressure on the rupee and which other channel?
x: Tightening abroad can cause capital outflows, rupee pressure and imported inflation through exchange-rate and import-cost channels.

s: Which one of the following correctly compares Andhra Pradesh’s retail inflation with the national rate mentioned for May 2026?
x: Andhra Pradesh’s CPI inflation was 4.9%, above the national rate of 3.9% mentioned for the comparison.

s: In June 2026, as major central banks geared up to tighten, what did the MPC do?
o: held the repo at 5.25% and cut the FY27 growth forecast
x: In June 2026 the MPC held 5.25% and cut the FY27 growth forecast.

s: Where was SBI's first overseas banking unit (OBU) set up?
x: SBI's first overseas banking unit was at Mumbai (asked in APPSC GS 2025).

s: By merging which banks was the Imperial Bank of India formed?
o: Punjab National Bank, Allahabad Bank and Canara Bank
Awadh Commercial Bank and Punjab National Bank
x: The Imperial Bank of India was formed by merging the three Presidency banks.

s: What was the rank of SBI, the only Indian bank in the top 100 global banks, in April 2024?
x: SBI ranked 47th in April 2024 (55th in April 2020).

s: On which date were the associate banks of the State Bank of India and Bharatiya Mahila Bank merged into SBI?
x: The associate banks of SBI and Bharatiya Mahila Bank were merged into SBI with effect from 1 April 2017.

s: In which year was the SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act passed?
x: The SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act came in 1959, after SBI (1955) and LIC (1956), and before the 1969 nationalisation.

s: In June 2007, the Government acquired what share of RBI's stake in SBI?
x: In June 2007 the Government acquired the RBI's 59.7% stake in SBI.

s: Under the SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959, how many princely-state banks became SBI associates?
x: The 1959 Act made eight princely-state banks associates of SBI.

s: When the State Bank of India was formed in 1955, what share of it did the RBI take?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (About 92%); it is added as option 5.
Many quiz sources and the app's earlier key: 60%. Library sources: RBI purchased 92% in 1955 (NextGen Indian Economy - APPSC 07 p.7; Ramesh Singh 10th ed. Part 5 p.83).
In the 1955 partial nationalisation the RBI bought about 92% of the Imperial Bank's shares (NextGen, Ramesh Singh); none of 51%, 60%, 74% or 100% fits, so 'About 92%' is added. The RBI's holding fell to 59.7% after SBI's 1993 share issue, and that 59.7% is the stake the Government took over in 2007.

s: Where is the head office of Equitas Small Finance Bank?
x: Equitas SFB is headquartered in Chennai; Capital SFB was established at Jalandhar.

s: Which of the following institutions was NOT founded by Dr Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya?
x: Dr Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded Andhra Insurance Company, Bharat Lakshmi Bank and the Krishna District Co-operative Bank. Punjab National Bank was established separately in 1894.

s: During which period was Dr. Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramaiah the President of the Indian National Congress?
x: Dr. Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramaiah was also INC President in 1948–49.

s: Andhra Bank, founded at Machilipatnam in 1923 by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya, was merged in 2020 into which bank?
x: Andhra Bank merged into Union Bank of India in 2020; Indian Bank absorbed Allahabad Bank.

s: Who founded Canara Bank at Mangaluru in 1906?
x: Ammembal Subba Rao Pai founded Canara Bank in 1906 at Mangaluru.

s: Lala Lajpat Rai was among the founders of which bank?
x: Lala Lajpat Rai was among the founders of Punjab National Bank (Lahore, 1894).

s: In which year did Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya found Andhra Insurance Co.?
x: He founded Andhra Insurance Co. in 1925, two years after Andhra Bank (1923).

s: Which bank has the tagline 'With You All The Way'?
x: 'With You All The Way' is the tagline of the State Bank of India.

s: Which bank received the Core Banking System Initiative Award in 2014?
x: Bharatiya Mahila Bank got the Core Banking System Initiative Award in 2014; it was merged into SBI in 2017.

s: With which bank did the private-sector Bank of Punjab merge in 2005?
x: Bank of Punjab, a private bank, merged with Centurion Bank in 2005.

s: With which bank was the Bank of Karad merged in 1994 after it closed following the securities scam?
x: Bank of Karad closed after the securities scam and was merged with Bank of India in 1994.

s: Which bank has the tagline 'Relationship beyond banking'?
x: 'Relationship beyond banking' is the tagline of Bank of India.

s: Which bank uses the tagline 'The name you can bank upon'?
x: 'The name you can bank upon' is Punjab National Bank's tagline.

s: The six banks nationalised on 15 April 1980 each had deposits of over how much?
x: The 1980 round covered banks with deposits above ₹200 crore; the 1969 round covered 14 banks with deposits above ₹50 crore.

s: Which of the following banks was NOT among those nationalised in 1980?
x: The 1980 round covered Andhra, Corporation, New Bank of India, OBC, Punjab & Sind and Vijaya Banks; Syndicate Bank was among those nationalised in 1969.

s: Which of the following was a significant result associated with bank nationalisation?
o: Exclusive lending to large industrial houses
Expansion of bank branches and growth of priority-sector lending
Withdrawal of institutional credit from agriculture
Reduction in branch expansion and contraction of rural banking
x: Bank nationalisation was associated with expansion of branches and increased lending to priority sectors, including agriculture and small units.

s: The 14 major commercial banks were nationalised under which legislation in 1969?
o: Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1969
x: The 14 banks were nationalised under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1969.

s: Towards which sectors was bank nationalisation in India mainly meant to shift credit?
x: Nationalisation aimed at social control of credit and a shift towards agriculture and small units, reducing industrial houses' control.

s: What was the minimum deposit size of each of the 14 banks nationalised in 1969?
x: The 1969 round covered banks with deposits of ₹50 crore and above; ₹200 crore was the 1980 threshold.

s: Who was the Prime Minister during the bank nationalisations of 1969 and 1980?
o: Indira Gandhi in 1969, Morarji Desai in 1980
Lal Bahadur Shastri in 1969, Indira Gandhi in 1980
Morarji Desai in 1969, Indira Gandhi in 1980
x: Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister in both rounds of nationalisation.

s: Which of the following was NOT among the 14 banks nationalised in 1969?
x: Vijaya Bank was nationalised in 1980; Canara, Syndicate and UCO were in the 1969 round.

s: In which year was Syndicate Bank nationalised?
x: Syndicate Bank was among the 14 banks nationalised in 1969, not in 1980.

s: On which date were six more commercial banks nationalised in India?
x: The second round on 15 April 1980 nationalised 6 banks with deposits of ₹200 crore and above; the first round was 19 July 1969.

s: What is the title of Indira Gandhi's note on bank nationalisation?
x: Indira Gandhi's note was titled 'Stray Thoughts on Bank Nationalisation'.

s: About what share of bank deposits was held by the 14 banks nationalised in 1969?
x: The 14 banks nationalised in 1969 held about 85% of deposits.

s: Which one of the following is a liability of a commercial bank?
x: Customer deposits are liabilities because the bank owes these amounts to depositors. Loans, investments and cash reserves are assets of the bank.

s: Since 1 April 2012, a cheque in India is valid for how long from its date of issue?
x: Since 1 April 2012, cheques have been valid for 3 months from the date of issue. The earlier validity was 6 months. 1 month and 12 months were never the general rule.

s: Which of the following activities is an example of para-banking?
o: Distributing mutual funds and providing insurance services
x: Para-banking refers to services beyond the traditional acceptance of deposits and provision of loans, including credit cards, insurance, factoring and mutual fund distribution. Credit to paramilitary personnel is not para-banking merely because of the category of borrower.

s: Which one of the following statements about the use of Aadhaar by banks is correct?
o: Aadhaar can be used for KYC verification with the customer's consent
Aadhaar must be used for KYC for every account, whether or not the customer consents
Aadhaar cannot be used for KYC verification by banks
Only payments banks may use Aadhaar for KYC verification
x: Banks can use Aadhaar for KYC verification with the customer's consent (APPSC-GS 2019). It is neither mandatory regardless of consent nor barred, and it is not limited to payments banks.

s: From 1 October 2021, what is a bank's penalty for an ATM out of cash for more than 10 hours in a month?
x: The RBI levies ₹10,000 per ATM that is out of cash for more than 10 hours in a month.

s: Under the Service Area Approach (1989), for which area does each rural bank branch prepare credit plans?
x: Under the Service Area Approach, each rural branch plans credit for a specified set of villages.

s: Which bank acts as the Lead Bank and SLBC convener in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Union Bank of India acts as the Lead Bank and the convener of the State Level Bankers’ Committee in Andhra Pradesh.

s: In whose recommendations did the Lead Bank Scheme originate?
x: The D.R. Gadgil Study Group (report October 1969) gave rise to the Lead Bank Scheme of December 1969.

s: The Lead Bank Scheme began in December 1969, the same year as which event?
x: The Lead Bank Scheme began in December 1969, the year 14 banks were nationalised.

s: Besides the D. R. Gadgil Study Group, which committee is linked to the origin of the Lead Bank Scheme?
x: The Lead Bank Scheme (Dec 1969) arose from the Gadgil Study Group and the Nariman Committee.

s: Under the Service Area Approach (April 1989), how many villages does each rural or semi-urban bank branch serve?
x: Each rural/semi-urban branch serves 15–25 villages under the Service Area Approach.

s: Which forum coordinates the Lead Bank Scheme at the State level?
x: The SLBC works at the State level; the Lead District Manager at the district level.

s: With which bank was Dena Bank, nationalised in 1969, later merged?
x: Dena Bank was merged with Bank of Baroda, not Bank of India.

s: Into which bank was Syndicate Bank, nationalised in 1969, merged?
x: Canara Bank took over Syndicate Bank.

s: On which date was the Life Insurance Corporation of India formed under the LIC Act, 1956?
x: LIC was formed on 1 September 1956 by merging over 240 insurers and societies; 19 July 1969 is when 14 banks were nationalised.

s:
Consider the following statements about C.D. Deshmukh:
1. He was the first Indian Governor of the RBI.
2. He served as Finance Minister from 1950 to 1956.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: C.D. Deshmukh was the first Indian RBI Governor and later Finance Minister (1950-56).

s: RBI was nationalised on which date under the RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948?
x: The RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949 under the RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948. 1 July 1955 is SBI, and 19 July 1969 the bank nationalisation.

s: In which year was the Banking Regulation Act enacted?
x: The Banking Regulation Act was passed in 1949, the same year the RBI was nationalised.

s: In which year was general insurance in India nationalised?
x: General insurance was nationalised in 1972; LIC came in 1956.

s: About how many insurers were merged to form the LIC in 1956?
x: LIC was formed on 1 September 1956 by merging more than 240 insurers.

s: Which of the following pairs (bank – bank into which it was merged) is correctly matched?
o: Oriental Bank of Commerce – Punjab National Bank
Vijaya Bank – Union Bank of India
United Bank of India – Canara Bank
x: OBC and United Bank went into PNB; Vijaya into Bank of Baroda; Corporation and Andhra Bank into Union Bank.

s: Which one of the following is regarded as the first bank in India?
x: Bank of Hindustan is regarded as the first bank in India. The Presidency Bank of Bengal was the first bank of the East India Company.

s: Which was the first bank with wholly Indian capital and management?
x: Punjab National Bank is described as the first bank with wholly Indian capital and management. Awadh Commercial Bank was the first bank run by Indians with limited liability and an all-Indian board.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
x: Awadh Commercial Bank was established at Faizabad in 1881. Andhra Bank was founded at Machilipatnam, Punjab National Bank at Lahore and Equitas Small Finance Bank has its head office at Chennai.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First small finance bank – Equitas Small Finance Bank
First bank run by Indians – Andhra Bank
First ATM – Central Bank of India
First private bank after 1994 liberalisation – UTI Bank (now Axis Bank)
x: UTI Bank, now Axis Bank, was the first private bank set up after the 1994 liberalisation. The first SFB was Capital SFB, the first bank run by Indians was Oudh Commercial Bank and the first ATM was HSBC's.

s: Which bank set up the first ATM in India in 1987?
x: HSBC set up India's first ATM in Mumbai in 1987.

s: Which bank issued India's first credit card in 1980?
x: Central Bank of India issued the first credit card in 1980.

s: Which was India's first small finance bank, which began in 2016?
x: Capital Small Finance Bank, Jalandhar (2016), was the first SFB.

s: Which was the first Presidency bank, set up in 1806?
x: The Bank of Calcutta (1806), later Bank of Bengal, was the first Presidency bank; Bombay (1840) and Madras (1843) followed.

s: Which was the oldest joint-stock bank of India, set up in 1865?
x: Allahabad Bank (1865) was the oldest joint-stock bank; it was later merged into Indian Bank.

s: In which year was Allahabad Bank, later merged into Indian Bank, established?
x: Allahabad Bank dates from 1865 and was merged into Indian Bank.

s:
Arrange the following Presidency banks in the order of their setting up:
1. Bank of Madras
2. Bank of Calcutta
3. Bank of Bombay
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Bank of Calcutta (1806), Bank of Bombay (1840) and Bank of Madras (1843); they later merged into the Imperial Bank (1921).

s: Which of the following about SBI and Regional Rural Banks is NOT correct?
o: SBI was formed from the Imperial Bank of India
The first RRB was set up on 2 October 1974
Prathama Grameen Bank was the first RRB
x: The first RRB, Prathama Grameen Bank, opened on 2 October 1975, not 1974.

s: On whose recommendation were Regional Rural Banks set up in 1975?
x: The Narasimham Working Group recommended RRBs in 1975; Prathama Grameen Bank was the first RRB.

s: What is the shareholding of a Regional Rural Bank among the Centre, the State Government and the sponsor bank?
x: RRBs follow a 50:15:35 shareholding among the Central Government, State Government and sponsor bank.

s: The Regional Rural Banks were initially created through an ordinance before being placed under which legislation?
x: Regional Rural Banks were initially created through an ordinance and were subsequently governed by the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976.

s: Regional Rural Banks are regulated by the RBI. By whom are they supervised?
x: RRBs are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India and supervised by NABARD.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Location of the first RRB – Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh
x: The first RRB was set up at Moradabad (UP); banks were nationalised first in 1969 and again in 1980.

s: Which of the following was NOT a location of the first five Regional Rural Banks (1975)?
x: The first five RRBs were at Moradabad, Malda, Gorakhpur, Bhiwani and Jaipur.

s: Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank was formed by merging how many RRBs of Andhra Pradesh?
x: It merged four AP RRBs: Andhra Pragathi, AP Grameena Vikas, Chaitanya Godavari and Saptagiri.

s: Under One State-One RRB, from 1 May 2025, to what number did RRBs fall from 43?
x: One State-One RRB reduced RRBs from 43 to 28.

s: In which year was the Nachiket Mor Committee, linked to differentiated banking licences, constituted?
x: The Nachiket Mor Committee was set up in 2013; Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks arose from such niche licences.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Small Finance Banks and Payments Banks?
o: A Payments Bank can undertake lending
A Small Finance Bank can undertake lending
A Payments Bank can accept only demand deposits, within a per-customer limit
A Small Finance Bank must direct 75% of its ANBC to the priority sector
x: Payments Banks cannot lend; they accept only demand deposits, while Small Finance Banks lend and must give 75% of ANBC to priority sectors.

s: What is the maximum deposit that a Payments Bank may presently accept from an individual customer?
x: The present maximum deposit limit for a customer of a Payments Bank is ₹2 lakh; the earlier limit was ₹1 lakh.

s: Payments banks in India are licensed under which provision?
o: Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
x: Payments banks are licensed under Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and are public limited companies under the Companies Act, 2013. Section 42 of the RBI Act governs CRR, Section 45ZB constitutes the MPC, and Section 24 of the BR Act governs SLR.

s: Under RBI norms of April 2024, what minimum net worth does a small finance bank moving to universal banking need?
x: The transition needs a net worth of at least ₹1,000 crore and a 5-year satisfactory track record.

s: Which small finance bank got RBI approval in 2025 to become a universal bank?
x: AU Small Finance Bank got approval in 2025 to transition to a universal bank.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about payments banks?
o: They keep 75% of demand deposits in SLR securities
They must maintain a CRAR of 15%
x: Payments banks cannot lend or issue credit cards; the other statements are correct.

s: A small finance bank must lend what share of its ANBC to the priority sector?
x: SFBs must lend 75% of ANBC to the priority sector; 40% is the target for domestic banks.

s: What minimum capital did the 2014 guidelines require for a small finance bank?
x: Under the 2014 guidelines a small finance bank needed minimum capital of ₹100 crore; ₹1,000 crore net worth is for moving to a universal bank.

s: The licence of which payments bank was cancelled by the RBI as harmful to depositors and the public?
x: The RBI cancelled Paytm Payments Bank's licence as harmful to depositors and the public.

s: Under small finance bank norms, at least what share of loans must be of up to ₹25 lakh?
x: SFBs must keep 50% of their loans at ₹25 lakh or less, besides 75% of ANBC to the priority sector.

s: Since which year have small finance bank licences been given on tap?
x: SFB licences are on tap since 2019.

s:
Consider the following statements about a small finance bank moving to a universal bank (RBI, April 2024):
1. It needs a satisfactory track record of 5 years.
2. It must change its promoters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The transition needs 5 years' satisfactory record and ₹1,000 crore net worth, with no change of promoters.

s: Up to what amount must bank loans to micro and small enterprises be given without collateral?
x: MSE loans up to ₹20 lakh and all PMEGP units must be collateral-free; banks may raise this limit to ₹25 lakh.

s: The total priority sector lending target for domestic banks is what share of ANBC?
x: Domestic banks must lend 40% of ANBC to the priority sector; 75% applies to SFBs and RRBs.

s: What is the agriculture sub-target under priority sector lending for domestic banks?
x: Agriculture gets 18% of ANBC, of which 10% is for small and marginal farmers.

s: Which of the following priority sector sub-targets (share of ANBC) is correctly matched?
x: Micro enterprises get 7.5%; weaker sections 12%, small and marginal farmers 10%, agriculture 18%.

s: On which RBI platform are Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs), introduced in 2016, traded?
x: PSLCs are traded on the RBI's e-Kuber platform; surplus banks sell them to banks with shortfalls.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's credit-deposit ratio in December 2025?
x: The ratio fell from 162% (Dec 2024) to 157.40% (Dec 2025), still well above the RBI norm of 60%.

s: At what level did gross NPAs of banks stand in September 2025, a multi-decadal low?
x: GNPA was 2.2% in September 2025, alongside the 4R strategy for public sector banks.

s: About how many PMJDY accounts were there in India in August 2026?
x: There were 58.77 crore PMJDY accounts in August 2026; 17.36 lakh is the number of BCs.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the highest credit-deposit ratio in December 2024?
x: Konaseema had the highest CD ratio (213%), then Nandyal (202%); Tirupati was the lowest (85%).

s: In August 2026, what share of villages in India had a banking outlet within 5 km?
x: 99.92% of villages had a banking outlet within 5 km.

s: About how many bank branches were there in India in August 2026?
x: India had about 1.81 lakh bank branches and 17.36 lakh business correspondents.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the lowest credit-deposit ratio in December 2024?
x: Tirupati had the lowest CD ratio (85%); Konaseema the highest (213%).

s: What was the total of bank deposits in Andhra Pradesh in December 2025?
x: AP deposits were ₹6,08,834 crore against credit of ₹9,58,277 crore (Dec 2025).

s: What strategy did the Government follow for cleaning up public sector banks?
x: The 4R strategy (recognition, resolution, recapitalisation, reform) was followed for PSBs.

s: Which principle is associated with the governance of co-operative banks?
x: Co-operative banks follow the principle of one member, one vote.

s: Scheduled banks are those listed in which Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934?
x: Scheduled banks are in the Second Schedule; they need paid-up capital and reserves of at least ₹5 lakh and can borrow from the RBI.

s: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation was formed in 1978 by merging which two institutions?
x: DICGC was formed in 1978 through the merger of the Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Credit Guarantee Corporation of India.

s: Which of the following belongs to the unorganised sector of Indian banking?
x: Indigenous bankers and moneylenders form the unorganised sector; the others are organised.

s: What minimum paid-up capital and reserves does a bank need to be a scheduled bank?
x: Scheduled banks, listed in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act 1934, need paid-up capital and reserves of at least ₹5 lakh.

s: Under the RBI framework of November 2013, what minimum capital does a foreign bank's wholly owned subsidiary need?
x: A WOS of a foreign bank needs minimum capital of ₹500 crore and gets near national treatment.

s:
Consider the following statements about NBFCs:
1. They cannot take demand deposits.
2. They cannot issue cheques.
3. Their deposits are insured by DICGC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NBFCs cannot take demand deposits or issue cheques, and they are not DICGC-insured.

s: What is a syndicated loan?
o: A single loan to one borrower funded by a group of lenders and arranged by a lead bank
A loan given by the RBI to a group of banks
A loan given by a cooperative society to a self-help group
A loan guaranteed by the Central Government
x: In a syndicated loan, a group (syndicate) of lenders funds one borrower; a lead bank arranges and manages it.

s: Which was India's first development finance institution, set up in 1948?
x: IFCI (1948) was the first DFI, for industrial finance.

s: Which of the following DFIs is correctly matched with its year of set-up?
x: SIDBI was set up in 1990; IDBI in 1964, EXIM Bank in 1982 and NaBFID in 2021.

s: For which sector is NaBFID, set up in 2021, a development finance institution?
x: NaBFID (2021) finances infrastructure; SIDBI serves MSMEs and EXIM Bank foreign trade.

s: Which DFI was set up in 1964 as the apex institution for industrial finance?
x: IDBI (1964) was the apex industrial finance institution.

s: Which committee recommended a three-tier banking structure and closure of weak and unviable banks?
x: Narasimham-II emphasised consolidation, a three-tier structure and resolution of weak banks; Narasimham-I recommended cutting SLR and CRR.

s: To what level did the Narasimham-II Committee (report April 1998) recommend raising CRAR?
x: Narasimham-II, the Committee on Banking Sector Reforms, recommended CRAR of 10%.

s: How many international banks did the three-tier banking structure suggested by Narasimham-II envisage?
x: It proposed two or three international banks, eight to ten national banks and many local banks.

s: With which committee was the idea of creating fewer and stronger banks through mergers particularly associated?
x: Narasimham-II recommended consolidation through mergers of strong banks and the creation of fewer, stronger banking institutions.

s: What was the official name of the Narasimham Committee-II (report April 1998)?
x: Narasimham-II was the Committee on Banking Sector Reforms; Narasimham-I (1991) was the Committee on the Financial System.

s: How many national banks did the three-tier structure of the Narasimham-II Committee envisage?
x: It envisaged 2-3 international banks, 8-10 national banks and many local banks.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Narasimham Committee-I (1991):
1. It recommended lower SLR and CRR.
2. It recommended ending dual control of banks.
3. It recommended raising CRAR to 10%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Narasimham-I sought lower SLR/CRR and an end to dual control; CRAR of 10% was a Narasimham-II recommendation.

s: What was the official name of the Narasimham Committee set up in 1991?
x: The 1991 Narasimham Committee was the Committee on the Financial System; the 1998 one was the Committee on Banking Sector Reforms.

s: Who was the chairman of the Committee on the Financial System set up in 1991?
x: The Committee on the Financial System (1991) was headed by M. Narasimham, a former RBI Governor.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Narasimham Committee of 1991 was officially called the Committee on the Financial System.
2. The Narasimham Committee of 1998 was officially called the Committee on Banking Sector Reforms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Narasimham-I (1991) was the Committee on the Financial System and Narasimham-II (1998) the Committee on Banking Sector Reforms.

s: What is the title of the report of the Raghuram Rajan Committee on Financial Sector Reforms?
x: The Raghuram Rajan Committee’s report was titled “A Hundred Small Steps.”

s: With which subject was the S.H. Khan Working Group of 1998 concerned?
o: Determining the contingent risk buffer of the RBI
Restructuring weak public sector banks through seven parameters
Setting up the Banks Board Bureau
Harmonising the roles of banks and Development Finance Institutions
x: The S.H. Khan Working Group examined how the roles of banks and Development Finance Institutions could be harmonised, leading towards universal banking.

s: With which subject is the Nachiket Mor Committee (2013) associated?
o: Small finance banks and payments banks
x: The Nachiket Mor Committee, constituted in 2013, examined differentiated banks, including small finance banks and payments banks.

s: With which subject did the Tarapore Committee-II (2006) deal?
x: Tarapore II (2006) was on fuller capital account convertibility; Tarapore I (1997) on capital account convertibility; Narasimham I and II on the financial system and banking reforms.

s: Who headed the Tax Reforms Committee of 1991?
x: Raja Chelliah headed the 1991 Tax Reforms Committee; Kelkar led the 2002 tax task forces and the PPP review.

s: With which subject did the Malhotra Committee deal?
x: Malhotra covered insurance reform; the Rangarajan committees covered financial inclusion, sugar decontrol and disinvestment.

s: In which year was the Vaghul Committee constituted?
x: The Vaghul Committee was set up in 1987 to study the money market (call money market). Narasimham I came in 1991, Narasimham II in 1997-98, and the Raghuram Rajan committee was formed in 2007.

s: With which subject did the Vaghul Committee deal?
x: Vaghul covered the call money market; Goswami industrial sickness, Janakiraman the stock-market scam and Abid Hussain SSI de-reservation.

s: With which subject did the Economic Capital Framework of the RBI, associated with Bimal Jalan, deal?
o: Merging strong banks and closing weak banks
Transfer of reserves and surplus to the Government
x: Bimal Jalan chaired the committee on the RBI’s Economic Capital Framework, including the issue of reserves and surplus transfer to the Government.

s: How many parameters were used for identifying weak banks by the M.S. Verma Committee?
x: The M.S. Verma Committee identified weak banks using seven parameters.

s: The Union Budget 2026–27 announced the restructuring of which institutions?
x: Budget 2026–27 announced restructuring of PFC and REC, along with a High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat.

s: With which subject did the Goiporia Committee deal?
x: Goiporia covered customer service in banks; Malhotra insurance, Rangarajan financial inclusion and P.J. Nayak bank-board governance.

s: With which subject did the Rangarajan Committee of 1993 deal?
x: The 1993 Rangarajan Committee dealt with disinvestment; the 2006 Rangarajan Committee dealt with financial inclusion.

s: With which subject did the S.S. Tarapore Committee of 1997 deal?
x: Tarapore-I (1997) dealt with capital account convertibility; Tarapore-II (2006) with fuller convertibility.

s: What did the P.J. Nayak Committee (2014), set up by the RBI, review?
x: P.J. Nayak reviewed governance of bank boards, leading to the Banks Board Bureau.

s: At what level was the Contingent Risk Buffer set under the Bimal Jalan panel's Economic Capital Framework?
x: The Jalan framework kept a Contingent Risk Buffer of 5.5-6.5%.

s: The Union Budget 2026-27 announced which committee to review the whole banking sector?
o: High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat
x: Budget 2026-27 announced a High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat.

s: With which subject is the Janakiraman Committee associated?
x: The Janakiraman Committee looked into the stock market scam; Goiporia dealt with customer service and Goswami with industrial sickness.

s: Which committee dealt with industrial sickness?
x: The Onkar Goswami Committee dealt with industrial sickness; Abid Hussain dealt with de-reservation of SSI items.

s: With which subject was the Abid Hussain Committee concerned?
x: The Abid Hussain Committee dealt with de-reservation of items reserved for small-scale industries.

s: Which body set up the Raghuram Rajan Committee on Financial Sector Reforms in 2007?
x: The Raghuram Rajan Committee was formed in 2007 by the Planning Commission and reported in 2008 ('A Hundred Small Steps').

s: Who chaired the Committee on Financial Sector Assessment (CFSA) set up in 2006?
x: The CFSA, set up in September 2006 by the Government in consultation with the RBI, was chaired by RBI Deputy Governor Rakesh Mohan.

s: With which subject was the Committee on Financial Sector Assessment (2006) concerned?
x: The CFSA made a comprehensive self-assessment of India's financial sector, covering stability, development and financial standards; its report came in 2009.

s: From which date did the merger of 10 public sector banks into 4 come into effect?
x: Ten public sector banks were merged into four with effect from 1 April 2020.

s: Which of the following was NOT an expected gain from the consolidation of public sector banks?
o: Creation of lenders capable of competing globally
Economies of scale and lower costs
Permanent elimination of all non-performing assets
Better capital utilisation and risk management
x: The expected gains included scale, lower costs, global-size lenders, better capital use and improved risk management. Permanent elimination of all NPAs was not stated as an expected gain.

s: To how many was the number of Public Sector Banks in India reduced after the 2020 mega consolidation?
x: The 2020 mergers cut the number of public sector banks to 12, from 27 in 2017.

s: Which of the following bank amalgamations is NOT correctly matched with the year it took effect?
o: SBI associates and Bharatiya Mahila Bank with SBI – 2017
Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank with Bank of Baroda – 2019
Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank with Union Bank of India – 2020
x: Allahabad Bank merged into Indian Bank in 2020, along with the Andhra-Corporation merger; the SBI merger was in 2017 and Dena-Vijaya in 2019.

s: In which year were five associate banks and Bharatiya Mahila Bank merged into SBI?
x: The SBI merger took place in 2017; New Bank of India joined PNB in 1993 and ten PSBs were merged into four in 2020.

s: New Bank of India merged into which bank because of financial distress?
x: The loss-making New Bank of India merged into Punjab National Bank in 1993, the first merger of two nationalised banks.

s: On which date did the merger of Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank into Bank of Baroda take effect?
x: The Bank of Baroda merger took effect on 1 April 2019; the 2020 mergers took effect on 1 April 2020 and the SBI merger on 1 April 2017.

s: With which bank were Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank merged?
x: Andhra and Corporation Banks went into Union Bank; Syndicate into Canara, Allahabad into Indian Bank, and OBC and United Bank into PNB.

s: Who founded Andhra Bank at Machilipatnam?
x: Andhra Bank was founded at Machilipatnam by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

s: With which bank was Syndicate Bank merged in the 2020 PSB merger?
x: Syndicate Bank went to Canara Bank; Andhra and Corporation went to Union Bank.

s: With which bank was Allahabad Bank merged in the 2020 PSB merger?
x: Allahabad Bank was merged into Indian Bank.

s: Which of the following merged bank – anchor bank pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Oriental Bank of Commerce – Punjab National Bank
United Bank of India – Punjab National Bank
Corporation Bank – Union Bank of India
x: Andhra Bank went to Union Bank of India, not Canara Bank.

s: How many public sector banks (including SBI) were there in 2017, before consolidation?
x: PSBs fell from 27 in 2017 to 12 in 2020.

s: On which date was the merger of 10 PSBs into 4 announced?
x: It was announced on 30 August 2019 and took effect on 1 April 2020.

s: Where was Andhra Bank founded in 1923?
x: Andhra Bank was founded at Machilipatnam in 1923 by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

s: In which year was Andhra Bank founded by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya?
x: Andhra Bank was set up at Machilipatnam in 1923; it merged into Union Bank of India on 1 April 2020.

s: The Basel Accords are framed by which of the following bodies?
o: International Organization of Securities Commissions under the BIS
Financial Stability Board under the International Monetary Fund
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision under the Bank for International Settlements
International Monetary Fund under the World Bank
x: The Basel Accords are formulated by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), which functions under the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).

s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the three pillars of Basel II?
o: Capital adequacy, monetary stability and deposit insurance
Credit risk, exchange-rate risk and sovereign risk
Liquidity coverage, stable funding and countercyclical lending
Minimum capital requirements, supervisory review and market discipline
x: Basel II rests on three pillars: minimum capital requirements, supervisory review and market discipline.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Basel III – 2010, stronger capital and regulation with risk management
Basel Committee – originally the Committee on Banking Regulations and Supervisory Practices
x: Basel II dates to 2004 and added supervisory review and market discipline; 1988 capital adequacy is Basel I.

s: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) was established in which year?
x: The BIS was established in 1930 and is described as the world's oldest international financial organisation.

s: From which date did India begin implementing Basel III norms?
x: India applied Basel III from 1 January 2013; Basel III was the response to the 2007-09 global financial crisis.

s: With which subject does the Basel Convention, administered by UNEP, deal?
x: The Basel Convention concerns hazardous wastes; the Basel Accords (BCBS/BIS) concern bank capital, liquidity and risk.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision:
1. It was set up against the background of international currency and banking disturbances.
2. The failure of Bankhaus Herstatt was an important trigger for its setting up.
3. It works under the UNEP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Basel Committee arose from currency and banking turmoil, triggered by the Herstatt failure (1974). It works under the BIS, not UNEP, which runs the Basel Convention.

s: Under which of the following was the leverage ratio first introduced?
x: The leverage ratio, LCR and NSFR first came with Basel III.

s: Into how many risk buckets did Basel I (1988) group assets?
x: Basel I used five risk buckets (0, 10, 20, 50 and 100%).

s: When was the Basel II framework finalised?
x: Basel II was proposed in June 1999 and its framework came in June 2004.

s: In which year was the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision set up?
x: BCBS was set up at the end of 1974 after the Herstatt failure; BIS dates from 1930.

s: Which is the world's oldest international financial organisation?
x: The BIS, set up in 1930 at Basel, is the oldest international financial organisation; the IMF and World Bank came in 1944-45.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS)?
x: The BIS, under which the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision works, is based at Basel, Switzerland.

s: Basel I (1988), which focused on credit risk, prescribed minimum capital of what share of risk-weighted assets?
x: Basel I addressed credit risk and set minimum capital at 8 per cent of risk-weighted assets (India prescribed 9 per cent).

s: India introduced CRAR in 1992. At what level did India prescribe CRAR under the Basel I framework?
x: India introduced CRAR in 1992 and prescribed it at 9 per cent under Basel I, one percentage point above the Basel minimum of 8 per cent.

s: Which of the following correctly defines Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) or CRAR?
o: Total capital divided by risk-weighted assets
Total deposits divided by total advances
Tier 1 capital divided by total non-risk-weighted exposure
Liquid assets divided by short-term liabilities
x: CAR or CRAR is calculated as capital divided by risk-weighted assets. The leverage ratio, in contrast, uses total non-risk-weighted exposure.

s: Which of the following may be included in a bank's Tier 2 capital?
x: Tier 2 has a mixed equity-debt character and may include subordinated debt; paid-up capital, reserves and undistributed profits are Tier 1 core equity.

s: In October 2025, the RBI proposed lower risk weights under Basel III for which of the following sectors?
x: In October 2025, the RBI proposed lower Basel III risk weights for MSMEs and real estate.

s: What is the main trigger of the countercyclical capital buffer introduced by the RBI in 2015?
x: The RBI introduced the countercyclical capital buffer framework in 2015, with the credit-to-GDP gap as its main trigger.

s: Which of the following macroprudential tools is wrongly matched?
o: Capital conservation buffer – 2.5 per cent over the minimum under Basel III
Risk weights – raised to cool risky lending such as unsecured consumer credit
LTV cap – limits a loan to a share of collateral value
Leverage ratio – limits a loan to a share of collateral value
x: The leverage ratio caps total exposure against Tier 1 capital; limiting a loan to a share of collateral value is the LTV cap.

s: Which of the following correctly presents the RBI norms for CET1, Tier 1 capital and total CRAR?
x: The RBI norms listed are CET1 5.5 per cent, Tier 1 capital 7 per cent and total CRAR 9 per cent.

s: What is the BCBS minimum for the Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio?
x: The BCBS minimums are CET1 4.5%, Tier 1 6%, capital conservation buffer 2.5% and countercyclical buffer 0–2.5%.

s: In what range does the countercyclical capital buffer, introduced in India in 2015, allow extra capital during credit booms?
x: The CCyB ranges from 0 to 2.5 per cent during credit booms; India has had the framework since 2015 but has not activated it.

s: For how long a stress period does the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) under Basel III require banks to hold enough high-quality liquid assets?
x: LCR covers a 30-day stress; the NSFR concerns stable funding over a one-year horizon.

s: How are highly rated corporate bonds classified for the purpose of the LCR?
x: Cash, government securities and central-bank reserves are Level 1 HQLA; highly rated corporate bonds are Level 2.

s: What is the RBI's minimum Tier 1 capital ratio under Basel III?
x: RBI requires Tier 1 of 7% (BCBS 6%); 5.5% is the RBI's CET1 norm.

s: What is the leverage ratio prescribed by the RBI for D-SIBs?
x: RBI prescribes 4% for D-SIBs and 3.5% for other banks, against the BCBS 3%.

s: Over what period does the Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) measure stable funding?
x: NSFR looks at a 1-year horizon; LCR covers a 30-day stress.

s: What is the capital conservation buffer under both BCBS and RBI norms?
x: Both BCBS and RBI set the capital conservation buffer at 2.5%.

s: What is the minimum total CRAR under BCBS norms and under RBI norms respectively?
x: BCBS sets 8% and the stricter RBI norm is 9%; 4.5% and 5.5% are the CET1 norms.

s: What does the leverage ratio under Basel III measure?
o: Tier 1 capital against total non-risk-weighted exposure
Stable funding available over one year
x: The leverage ratio is Tier 1 capital divided by total exposure that is not risk-weighted; it caps lending against own capital.

s: What is the minimum leverage ratio prescribed by the RBI for banks other than D-SIBs?
x: The RBI prescribes a 4% leverage ratio for D-SIBs and 3.5% for other banks; the BCBS minimum is 3%.

s: Which ratio is used as a standard measure of the strength of a bank's balance sheet against its risk-weighted assets?
x: CRAR is capital divided by risk-weighted assets and measures the strength of banks' balance sheets.

s: What was the size of the public sector bank recapitalisation package announced in October 2017?
x: The October 2017 package was ₹2.11 lakh crore, of which ₹1.35 lakh crore came through recapitalisation bonds.

s: Indradhanush, introduced in August 2015, was primarily associated with which of the following reforms?
o: A seven-point plan for capitalisation and governance reform of public sector banks
A fiscal-deficit reduction programme for the Union Government
A scheme for consolidation of Regional Rural Banks
A framework for regulating private insurance companies
x: Indradhanush was a seven-point plan introduced in August 2015 for capital infusion and governance reform in public sector banks.

s: How do recapitalisation bonds support public sector banks without requiring an equivalent immediate cash outgo from the Union budget?
o: The Government transfers its tax receipts directly to bank depositors
The Government writes off all outstanding bank loans through monetary creation
Banks issue equity directly to the Reserve Bank of India without Government involvement
The Government issues bonds to banks and invests the proceeds back into them as equity
x: Under the mechanism, the Government issues bonds to public sector banks and puts the money back into them as equity; therefore, no equivalent fresh cash leaves the budget immediately.

s: What does the '4R' strategy adopted for cleaning up public sector banks stand for?
x: The 4R strategy is Recognition (of NPAs), Resolution, Recapitalisation and Reforms. The other options swap in terms such as Recovery, Restructuring, Regulation, Refinance and Reorganisation, which are not part of the official 4Rs.

s: What did the P.J. Nayak Committee propose to create to hold the Government's stake in public sector banks?
x: The committee proposed a Bank Investment Company, cutting the Government's stake below 50% and professional PSB boards.

s: With which initiative was the Banks Board Bureau, established in 2016, associated?
x: The Banks Board Bureau originated from the Indradhanush initiative and began functioning in 2016.

s: Which body replaced the Banks Board Bureau in 2022?
x: The Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) replaced the Banks Board Bureau in 2022.

s: How many points did the Indradhanush plan (2015) for public sector banks have?
x: Indradhanush was a 7-point plan (A-G), from Appointments to Governance.

s: What was the budget capital for PSBs over four years under Indradhanush?
x: Indradhanush provided ₹70,000 crore of budget capital over 4 years.

s: Of the ₹2.11 lakh crore PSB recapitalisation package of 2017, how much came through recapitalisation bonds?
x: ₹1.35 lakh crore came via recap bonds; about ₹58,000 crore was to be raised by banks.

s: What level of Government stake in PSBs did the P.J. Nayak Committee recommend?
x: P.J. Nayak proposed a Bank Investment Company and a Government stake below 50%.

s: From when did the Banks Board Bureau start working?
x: The BBB, an Indradhanush idea, began work on 1 April 2016.

s: On the recommendation of which committee was the Banks Board Bureau set up?
x: The P.J. Nayak Committee (2014) on governance of bank boards proposed the Banks Board Bureau, which began in April 2016.

s: What was the main function of the Banks Board Bureau?
o: Selecting chairmen and whole-time directors of public sector banks
x: The Banks Board Bureau selected PSB chairmen and whole-time directors and boards of PSU insurers and FIs.

s:
Assertion (A): The EASE Index ranks participating public sector banks on reform performance.
Reason (R): The index benchmarks mid-size and large public sector banks against reform themes every quarter.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true. Quarterly benchmarking of mid-size and large public sector banks against reform themes provides the basis for ranking them in the EASE Index.

s: What are the four focus areas of EASE 8.0, also called 'EASE ₹ise', for FY2026?
o: Risk and Resilience, Innovation, Socio-economic impact, Excellence
x: EASE 8.0 or EASE ₹ise focuses on Risk and Resilience, Innovation, Socio-economic impact and Excellence.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EASE (Enhanced Access and Service Excellence)?
o: It was conceptualised in 2015 and launched in 2017
It is governed by a board of heads of premier financial institutions
It became the PSB Reforms Agenda from January 2018
PSBs report quarterly against its benchmarks, overseen by IBA's EASE Steering Committee
x: EASE is run by the Indian Banks' Association's EASE Steering Committee, not a board of heads of premier financial institutions.

s: In which year were the EASE reforms for public sector banks launched?
x: EASE was conceptualised in 2015 and launched in 2017.

s: Which body runs the EASE reforms for public sector banks?
o: A board of heads of premier financial institutions
x: EASE is run by the IBA's EASE Steering Committee, not a board of FI heads (APPSC G1 2024).

s: What is the full form of EASE in the context of public sector bank reforms?
o: Easy Access to Savings and Equity
x: EASE stands for Enhanced Access and Service Excellence, the reform agenda for PSBs launched in 2017.

s: What does the EASE Index measure?
o: Performance of public sector banks on reforms
Ease of doing business for MSMEs
x: The EASE Index benchmarks and ranks public sector banks on reform performance; it does not measure MSME ease of doing business.

s: What was a major change in the regulatory structure of banking after the financial sector reforms?
o: SEBI assumed direct control over all public sector banks
The Finance Ministry’s Banking Division became the sole regulator of banks
The Banks Board Bureau replaced the RBI as the monetary authority
The RBI became the primary regulator and dual control with the Finance Ministry’s Banking Division ended
x: The RBI became the primary regulator, ending dual control with the Finance Ministry’s Banking Division. The reforms also promoted greater autonomy for public sector banks.

s: Up to what limit was FDI allowed in private sector banks in India in 2004?
x: FDI up to 74% in private banks was permitted in 2004; prudential norms and CRAR came in 1992.

s: In which year was the Banking Ombudsman introduced in India?
x: The Banking Ombudsman came in 1995; SEBI became statutory in 1992.

s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the financial-sector reforms initiated after 1991?
x: The FRBM Act, 2003 was a fiscal reform, not a financial-sector reform. The other three were components of post-1991 financial-sector reforms.

s: Which of the following pairs of post-1991 reforms and years is correctly matched?
o: Insurance opened by the IRDA Act - 2003
x: The exchange rate became market-determined in 1993. FEMA replaced FERA in 1999, not 1991. The IRDA Act was passed in 1999; 2003 is the FRBM Act, which is a fiscal reform. SEBI became statutory in 1992.

s: What was the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) in 1991-92?
x: SLR was 38.5% in 1991-92; cutting CRR and SLR was a key reform.

s: In which year did FEMA replace FERA?
x: FEMA replaced FERA in 1999, the year the IRDA Act opened insurance.

s: In which year was SEBI made a statutory body?
x: SEBI was made statutory in 1992, along with prudential norms and CRAR.

s: Which of the following were among the new private sector banks that entered after the 1991 reforms?
o: Bank of Baroda and Vijaya Bank
x: Private bank entry was a post-1991 reform; HDFC and ICICI banks came up by 1995, while the others are nationalised banks.

s: To how many did the number of Regional Rural Banks come down after the 2020–21 consolidation?
x: There were originally 196 RRBs; the 2020–21 consolidation brought the number down to 43.

s: On which date did the One State-One RRB arrangement, amalgamating 15 RRBs, become effective?
x: One State-One RRB took effect on 1 May 2025 (notified 8 April 2025): 26 RRBs were amalgamated, cutting RRBs from 43 to 28 – the stem's '15' is the net reduction, not the number amalgamated.

s: How many Regional Rural Banks were there originally, before consolidation?
x: RRBs fell from 196 originally to 43 and then 28.

s: How many Regional Rural Banks were there after One State-One RRB?
x: One State-One RRB brought the number down to 28 (May 2026).

s:
Consider the following statements about One State-One RRB:
1. It took effect on 1 May 2025.
2. Under it, the Centre gave up its 50% share in RRBs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: It took effect on 1 May 2025; the Centre keeps its 50% share.

s:
Consider the following statements about Regional Rural Banks:
1. A Regional Rural Bank is sponsored by a commercial bank.
2. The Central Government holds a 50% share in Regional Rural Banks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Each RRB is sponsored by a commercial bank, and the Centre keeps its 50% share even after consolidation.

s: Which of the following holds the largest share in the capital of a Regional Rural Bank?
x: The Central Government holds 50% of RRB capital; the sponsor bank and the State hold the rest.

s: Of which institution is the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) a wholly owned subsidiary?
x: DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India.

s: Which of the following deposits IS covered by DICGC deposit insurance?
o: Deposits in Indian branches of foreign banks
x: DICGC covers all commercial banks including foreign bank branches in India; inter-bank, NBFC and government deposits are excluded.

s: To what amount did the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 raise the 'substantial interest' threshold from ₹5 lakh?
x: The threshold rose from ₹5 lakh to ₹2 crore; the Act also raised co-operative bank directors' tenure from 8 to 10 years.

s: In which year's Budget was the DICGC deposit insurance limit raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh?
x: The deposit insurance limit was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in the 2020–21 Budget, following the PMC Bank crisis.

s: With regard to DICGC insurance, who bears the premium burden?
o: The insured bank, and not the depositor
RBI and the depositor in equal shares
x: Banks pay the DICGC insurance premium; the depositor does not pay it.

s: Under which Act does the DICGC function?
x: DICGC works under the DICGC Act, 1961; the corporation itself was formed in 1978.

s: After which crisis was the DICGC cover raised to ₹5 lakh?
x: The cover was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in Budget 2020-21 after the PMC Bank crisis.

s: To how many years did the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 raise the tenure of co-operative bank directors from 8 years?
x: The Act raised co-operative bank directors' tenure from 8 to 10 years.

s: On which date did the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 come into force?
x: The Act came into force on 1 August 2025.

s: In which year was the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) set up?
x: The DICGC was formed in 1978 by merging the Deposit Insurance Corporation (1962) and the Credit Guarantee Corporation.

s: What is the deposit insurance cover given by the DICGC per depositor per bank?
x: Since Budget 2020-21 the DICGC covers ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, up from ₹1 lakh.

s: In the debate over privatising public sector banks, what is the main argument for public ownership?
o: Social mandates such as rural branches and priority lending
x: The debate weighs possible efficiency and governance gains from privatisation against the social mandate of PSBs, including rural branches and priority lending.

s: Which of the following is cited as a criticism of public sector bank privatisation by trade unions?
o: It would make recapitalisation unnecessary in every case
It would weaken priority sector lending, rural credit and financial inclusion
It would increase the number of rural branches automatically
It would eliminate all integration costs arising from mergers
x: Trade unions have argued that privatisation could weaken priority sector lending, rural credit and financial inclusion.

s: LIC acquired a majority stake in IDBI Bank in 2019. What was the consequence of this transaction for the regulatory classification of IDBI Bank?
o: It was reclassified by RBI as a private sector lender
It was classified as a foreign bank subsidiary
It was converted into a cooperative bank
It was classified by RBI as a regional rural bank
x: Following LIC’s acquisition of a majority stake in 2019, RBI reclassified IDBI Bank as a private sector lender.

s: Which of the following was announced for privatisation in the Union Budget 2021–22?
o: Three public sector banks and one general insurance company
Two private banks and one public sector insurer
One public sector bank and two life insurance companies
Two public sector banks and one general insurance company
x: The Budget 2021–22 announced the privatisation of two public sector banks and one general insurance company.

s: What stake in IDBI Bank is on sale in its disinvestment?
x: A 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank is on sale.

s: Which of the following asset classifications is correctly matched?
o: Standard asset – NPA for more than 12 months
Sub-standard asset – NPA for more than 12 months
Sub-standard asset – NPA for 12 months or less
x: A sub-standard asset is an NPA for 12 months or less; an NPA for more than 12 months is doubtful.

s: What is the overdue period of a Special Mention Account classified as SMA-1?
x: SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2 cover 1–30, 31–60 and 61–90 overdue days; SMAs are early-warning accounts, not yet NPAs.

s: For how long must a loan for a short-duration crop remain overdue to become an NPA?
x: Agricultural loans become NPAs after two crop seasons for short-duration crops and one crop season for long-duration crops.

s: For how long must an asset have been an NPA to be classified as doubtful?
x: A doubtful asset has been an NPA for more than 12 months.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Special Mention Accounts?
o: SMA-0 covers overdue up to 30 days
An SMA-2 account is an NPA
SMA accounts are still standard assets
x: SMA-2 (61-90 days) is still a standard asset; an NPA needs overdue beyond 90 days.

s: For how long must a loan for a long-duration crop remain overdue to become an NPA?
x: Long-duration crop loans become NPAs after 1 crop season overdue; short-duration ones after 2.

s: What is an asset called whose loss has been identified by the bank, auditors or RBI inspection but which has not been wholly written off?
x: Such an asset is a loss asset.

s: After how long an overdue period does a loan become a Non-Performing Asset in India?
x: A loan becomes an NPA when its interest or principal stays overdue for more than 90 days.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A loan becomes an NPA when its interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days.
2. An SMA-2 account, overdue for 61-90 days, is classified as an NPA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The NPA cut-off is more than 90 days; SMA-2 accounts (61-90 days) are still standard assets.

s: For more than how many days must interest or principal remain overdue for a loan to become a Non-Performing Asset?
x: An NPA is a loan whose interest or principal is overdue for more than 90 days; SMA-0/1/2 (up to 90 days) are still standard.

s: How is an NPA that has remained sub-standard for more than 12 months classified?
x: A sub-standard asset is an NPA for up to 12 months; beyond 12 months it becomes doubtful. A loss asset is one identified but not written off.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about asset classification of bank loans?
o: SMA-2 accounts are still standard assets
A sub-standard asset is an NPA for up to 12 months
A loss asset is identified but not yet written off
SMA-0 accounts are classified as NPAs
x: SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2 accounts (overdue up to 90 days) are still standard assets, not NPAs.

s: How is the Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR) of a borrower calculated?
x: ICR = operating earnings (EBIT) divided by interest due; it indicates a borrower's present and emerging risk.

s: What does evergreening of loans mean?
o: Writing off all old loans immediately
Converting all NPAs into equity automatically
Giving fresh loans to repay old loans and conceal default
x: Evergreening involves extending fresh loans to repay old loans, thereby keeping the underlying default hidden.

s: Besides NPAs, what do the stressed assets of a bank include?
x: Stressed assets = NPAs + restructured loans + written-off assets.

s: How is Net NPA calculated?
o: Gross NPA divided by total advances
x: Net NPA is gross NPA minus provisions; provisions divided by gross NPA is the PCR.

s: An interest coverage ratio below 1 means that a borrower:
o: Has an NPA of over 90 days
Cannot cover its interest from earnings
x: ICR = EBIT / interest due; below 1 means earnings cannot cover interest.

s: An Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR) below 1 means the firm:
o: Cannot service its interest from earnings
x: ICR = EBIT ÷ interest payable; below 1, earnings do not cover interest.

s: What is meant by ‘evergreening’ of loans?
o: Writing off an old loan after full recovery
Giving a fresh loan to repay an old loan so that the NPA remains hidden
Increasing the maturity of a standard loan without any new borrowing
Converting every NPA into a government-guaranteed bond
x: Evergreening occurs when fresh loans are used to repay old loans, thereby concealing the underlying NPA.

s: How is the Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR) of a firm calculated?
x: ICR = EBIT ÷ interest payable; provisions ÷ gross NPA is the Provision Coverage Ratio.

s: When is interest on an NPA booked as income under income-recognition norms?
o: Only when it is actually received
After the asset is written off
When it is accrued, whether or not received
x: Interest on an NPA is not recognised as income until it is actually received. This forms part of the IRACP framework.

s: How is the Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) of a bank calculated?
x: PCR is provisions held divided by gross NPAs; Gross NPA minus provisions gives Net NPA.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the new borrower-level NPA tagging system?
o: Banks must identify NPAs through automated systems
It is to be effective from 1 April 2027
If one loan of a borrower becomes an NPA, all its loans at that bank become NPAs
An account can be upgraded even if arrears on one facility remain unpaid
x: An account is upgraded only after all arrears on every facility are paid.

s: Under its new provisioning framework, the RBI is moving from which approach to which approach?
o: From a 3-stage ECL model to a 2-stage incurred-loss model
From incurred-loss model to a 3-stage Expected Credit Loss model
From a 90-day overdue test to a 180-day overdue test
x: The RBI is shifting from the incurred-loss model to a forward-looking 3-stage Expected Credit Loss (ECL) model; the 90-day overdue test stays.

s: Under the Expected Credit Loss model, what provisioning do Stage 2 assets require?
x: Stage 2 assets need provisioning for lifetime expected loss; 12-month expected loss applies to Stage 1.

s: What do the IRACP norms of banks stand for?
x: IRACP = Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning.

s: From which date do the RBI's borrower-level NPA tagging and ECL model take effect?
x: Both new rules start on 1 April 2027.

s: Under borrower-level NPA tagging, when are an NPA borrower's accounts upgraded?
o: Arrears on the defaulted loan alone are paid
All arrears on every facility are paid
x: Upgrade comes only after all arrears on every facility are cleared.

s: A higher Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) indicates a bank that is:
x: PCR = provisions ÷ gross NPA; a higher PCR means more bad loans are provided for, so the bank is more resilient.

s: What does the twin balance sheet problem refer to?
o: High exports and low public debt
Fiscal surplus and excess bank liquidity
High household savings and low inflation
Over-leveraged corporates and capital-starved, NPA-laden banks
x: The twin balance sheet problem describes over-leveraged firms alongside capital-starved banks burdened with NPAs.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the twin balance sheet problem?
o: Private investment can decline as a result
Banks may freeze new lending rather than recall old loans
Over-leveraged firms can undertake fresh investment without difficulty
x: Over-leveraged firms find it hard to invest, which is why private investment falls.

s: Which Economic Survey prominently framed the twin balance sheet problem?
x: The Economic Survey 2016–17, under Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian, discussed the festering twin balance sheet problem.

s: Under which Chief Economic Adviser was the Economic Survey 2016-17, which framed the twin balance sheet problem, prepared?
x: The Survey of 2016-17 under CEA Arvind Subramanian named the twin balance sheet problem.

s: In the twin balance sheet problem, what does banks stopping new loans ultimately lead to?
o: A rise in corporate leverage capacity
x: Loan losses eat bank capital, banks stop lending, firms cannot invest, and private investment falls.

s: What does the 'twin balance sheet' problem refer to?
o: Rising fiscal and current account deficits
Stressed NBFCs and stressed microfinance institutions
x: The twin balance sheet problem is the combination of over-leveraged corporates and capital-starved banks.

s: To which sectors did the aggressive bank lending of 2010-15 that later turned into NPAs largely go?
x: Lending in 2010-15 went largely to infrastructure, steel and power without strict appraisal, leading to stalled projects.

s: In the NPA vicious cycle, what does the accumulation of NPAs lead to directly?
x: Aggressive lending and shocks create NPAs, which require provisioning and erode capital, resulting in weak credit growth.

s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of NPAs:
1. Aggressive lending in 2010-15 went to infrastructure, steel and power.
2. The 2008 global crisis and weak exports added to the stress.
3. Evergreening hid defaults.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: aggressive lending to infra, steel and power, global shocks and evergreening fed the NPA build-up.

s: In which year did the RBI carry out the Asset Quality Review?
x: The RBI conducted the Asset Quality Review in 2015.

s: What did the Government's 4R strategy in response to the banking-sector stress consist of?
x: The four Rs were Recognise, Resolve, Recapitalise and Reform. The response included the IBC, recapitalisation and NARCL.

s: Which of the following was used under the 4R strategy for stressed assets?
x: The 4R strategy worked with the IBC, recapitalisation and NARCL.

s: Which problem did the RBI's Asset Quality Review of 2015 expose?
x: The AQR showed NPAs jumping and exposed the twin balance sheet problem.

s: When did the GNPA ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks reach its peak of about 11.2 per cent?
x: SCB GNPA peaked at approximately 11.2 per cent in March 2018, after the Asset Quality Review.

s: What were the GNPA and NNPA ratios of Scheduled Commercial Banks in March 2026?
x: In March 2026, GNPA was 1.93 per cent and NNPA was 0.39 per cent, described as a decadal low.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank in FY26?
o: Its NNPA was reported as nil
Its NNPA was higher than its GNPA
x: Its GNPA was 0.91% and its NNPA nil, so the NNPA was lower, not higher, than the GNPA.

s: What was the GNPA ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks in March 2015, before the AQR?
x: GNPA was 4.28% in March 2015, peaked near 11.2% in 2018 and fell to 1.93% by March 2026.

s: The GNPA ratio of public sector banks fell from 4.97% in March 2015 to what in March 2025?
x: PSB GNPA fell from 4.97% to 2.58% between March 2015 and March 2025.

s: What was the GNPA ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks in September 2025?
