x: SCB GNPA was 2.15% in September 2025 and fell further to a decadal low of 1.93% (NNPA 0.39%) in March 2026; 11.2% was the March 2018 peak and 4.28% the March 2015 level.

s: How was the March 2026 SCB Gross NPA ratio of 1.93 per cent described?
x: The March 2026 Gross NPA ratio of 1.93 per cent was described as a decadal low.

s: Which of the following is NOT cited as a reason for the decline in banks' NPAs?
x: The fall in NPAs is credited to the 4R strategy, higher (not lower) provisioning, the IBC and NARCL, so lower provisioning requirements is not a reason.

s: In which year was the Asset Quality Review (AQR), which exposed the evergreening of bank loans, conducted?
x: The RBI's Asset Quality Review of 2015 exposed evergreening that had hidden NPAs.

s: What was the Net NPA ratio of scheduled commercial banks in March 2026?
x: In March 2026 SCB Gross NPA was 1.93% and Net NPA 0.39%, a decadal low.

s: Which of the following earlier debt-resolution mechanisms was introduced first?
x: Corporate Debt Restructuring came in 2001, followed by the 5/25 scheme (2014), Strategic Debt Restructuring (2015) and S4A (2016).

s: In which year did the RBI introduce the Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets (S4A)?
x: S4A came in 2016 and split a stressed firm's debt into sustainable and unsustainable parts; 2018 is Project Sashakt.

s: On the recommendations of which committee was Project Sashakt (2018) for resolving stressed assets based?
x: Project Sashakt came from the Sunil Mehta Committee; its plan binds all lenders once 66% approve, with the lead bank driving it.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RBI's Prudential Framework for Resolution of Stressed Assets?
o: Lenders must review the borrower account within 30 days of default
Signing an Inter-Creditor Agreement is voluntary
x: The framework makes the Inter-Creditor Agreement mandatory, not voluntary; it also requires a 30-day review and resolution within 180 days.

s: Under the Strategic Debt Restructuring (SDR) scheme of 2015, at least what share of equity could lenders acquire by converting debt?
x: SDR (2015) let lenders convert debt into 51% or more equity and take control of the firm.

s: What did the 5/25 scheme of 2014 provide for?
o: Splitting of debt into sustainable and unsustainable parts
Infrastructure loans amortised over 25 years and refinanced every 5 years
x: The 5/25 scheme let infrastructure loans run over 25 years with refinancing every 5 years; 51% equity was SDR and the debt split was S4A.

s: Under the Inter-Creditor Agreement of July 2018, approval by lenders holding what share makes a resolution plan binding on all lenders?
x: The ICA under Project Sashakt (33 banks, loans of ₹50 crore+) binds all lenders once 66% approve.

s: Under the IBC waterfall mechanism, which of the following ranks above government dues?
x: Resolution costs, workmen's dues and secured creditors' claims are placed above government dues in the IBC waterfall.

s: On the recommendations of which committee was the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 based?
x: The IBC came from the T.K. Viswanathan (Bankruptcy Law Reforms) Committee, 2015; Narasimham is linked to SARFAESI.

s: Which change in the control structure of insolvency proceedings was introduced by the IBC?
x: The IBC shifted the framework from debtor-in-possession to creditor-in-control.

s: A promoter classified as a wilful defaulter, or a promoter associated with an NPA, is generally barred from bidding under which provision of the IBC?
x: Section 29A prevents wilful defaulters and promoters of NPAs from submitting resolution bids, subject to the statutory framework.

s: What is the minimum default required to trigger the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP)?
x: CIRP needs a default of at least Rs 1 crore; it can be triggered by financial or operational creditors.

s: What is the outer time limit for completing CIRP, including litigation?
x: CIRP ordinarily runs 180 days with extension, with an outer limit of 330 days including litigation; actual cases have often taken longer.

s: When was the Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process for MSMEs introduced, and with what time limit?
x: The PPIRP for MSMEs was introduced in 2021 and has a 120-day limit.

s: To what has the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026 cut the liquidation timeline?
x: Liquidation is cut to 180 + 90 days; the Act also adds the hybrid Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process (Secs 54C–54P).

s: Within how many days must the NCLT admit or reject a CIRP plea under the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026?
x: The 2026 amendment requires admission or rejection within 14 days; resolution plans must be ruled on within 30 days.

s: The IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026 changed 'may' to 'shall' in Section 7(5)(a) of the Code. Which ruling did this change overturn?
o: Lalit Kumar Jain v. Union of India
Swiss Ribbons v. Union of India
x: The change from 'may' to 'shall' in Sec 7(5)(a) makes admission of a financial creditor's CIRP plea mandatory once default is proved, overturning the Vidarbha Industries ruling, which had read 'may' as giving the NCLT discretion. Lalit Kumar Jain (2021) concerns personal guarantors' liability; Swiss Ribbons and Essar Steel are other IBC judgments not affected by this change.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes insolvency from bankruptcy?
o: Bankruptcy is the inability to pay debts as they fall due, whereas insolvency is a court-approved resolution plan
Insolvency is a legal declaration, whereas bankruptcy is a financial state
Insolvency is the inability to pay debts as they fall due, whereas bankruptcy is the legal declaration or process that follows
Both insolvency and bankruptcy refer exclusively to liquidation of companies
x: Insolvency is the financial state of being unable to pay debts when due. Bankruptcy is the legal declaration or process that follows insolvency.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about personal guarantors in insolvency?
o: Personal guarantors remain liable after approval of a resolution plan
The Supreme Court affirmed it in 2021
The principle was affirmed in Lalit Kumar Jain v. Union of India
Approval of a resolution plan automatically releases every personal guarantor
x: Approval of a resolution plan does not automatically release guarantors; they remain liable, as affirmed in Lalit Kumar Jain (2021).

s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or debate concerning the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code?
x: Protracted litigation, limited NCLT capacity, deep haircuts and guarantor liability are identified concerns. The Code has not eliminated guarantor liability.

s: Under the IBC, which body votes on the resolution plan of a corporate debtor?
x: During CIRP, the Committee of Creditors votes on the resolution plan; the NCLT adjudicates.

s: Within how many days must the Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process (CIIRP) under the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026 be completed?
x: CIIRP has a 150-day timeline and needs 51% creditors; CIRP has 330 days and PPIRP 120 days.

s: The IBC 2016 replaced which earlier law under which the BIFR functioned?
x: The IBC replaced the Sick Industrial Companies Act (SICA) 1985 and the BIFR.

s: Which law was enacted in India in May 2016 on the recommendation of the T.K. Viswanathan Committee?
o: Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act
x: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code was enacted on 28 May 2016 on the T.K. Viswanathan Committee's report.

s: What mainly shows the deterrent effect of the IBC?
o: Completion of all cases by NCLT within 330 days
Settlement of a large number of cases before admission
Transfer of all recovery cases to Lok Adalats
x: The settlement of 30,310 cases worth ₹13.78 lakh crore before admission was cited as evidence of the IBC's deterrent effect.

s: In the context of banking supervision, what is the full form of PCA?
x: PCA stands for Prompt Corrective Action, a framework used by the Reserve Bank of India to intervene in banks with weakening financial health.

s: Under the Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework, which body may order capital infusion, a change of management or a merger?
x: Under PCA, the RBI may restrict lending, branch expansion, dividends and pay, and may order capital infusion, a management change or a merger.

s: In which year did the Reserve Bank of India introduce the Prompt Corrective Action framework?
x: The RBI introduced the Prompt Corrective Action framework in 2002 to monitor and restrict banks whose financial metrics deteriorate.

s: Which of the following pairs of PCA trigger parameter and indicator is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Asset quality is assessed through the net NPA ratio; the Tier-1 leverage ratio measures leverage.

s: Which of the following is NOT a trigger parameter under the RBI's Prompt Corrective Action framework?
x: The PCA triggers are capital (CRAR/CET1), asset quality (net NPA) and leverage (Tier 1 leverage ratio).

s: Which of the following is a restriction that may be imposed on a bank under PCA?
o: Mandatory listing on a stock exchange
x: Under PCA the RBI may curb lending, branch expansion, dividends and management pay.

s: When was the RBI's Prompt Corrective Action framework of 2002 last revised?
x: PCA was introduced by the RBI in 2002 and revised in November 2021.

s: The RBI's Prompt Corrective Action framework is applied mainly to check which of the following?
o: Weak banks with high NPAs and low capital
Fiscal deficit of the Union government
x: PCA lets the RBI restrict banks that breach thresholds on capital, asset quality (net NPA) and leverage.

s: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) replaced the Company Law Board, the BIFR and which other body?
x: NCLT replaced the Company Law Board, BIFR and AAIFR; it did not replace the Securities Appellate Tribunal.

s: Which authority is the adjudicating authority for corporate insolvency under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
x: The NCLT is the adjudicating authority for corporate insolvency under the IBC, 2016. The DRT is the authority for individuals and partnership firms.

s: Where is the NCLT bench in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The NCLT bench sits at Amaravati, while the DRT bench is at Visakhapatnam.

s: The NCLAT hears appeals against orders of the NCLT, IBBI, CCI and which other body?
x: The NCLAT hears appeals against orders of the NCLT (Sec 61 of the IBC), the IBBI, the CCI and the NFRA; its own orders go to the Supreme Court.

s: Under which provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 are the NCLT and NCLAT respectively set up?
x: NCLT is established under Section 408 and NCLAT under Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013.

s: Where does the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) sit?
x: NCLAT sits in New Delhi and Chennai and hears appeals from NCLT under Section 61 of the IBC.

s: What does the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) regulate?
x: IBBI regulates insolvency professionals, insolvency professional agencies, information utilities and registered valuers.

s: Under the IBC, which is the adjudicating authority for insolvency of individuals and partnership firms?
x: The DRT handles individuals and partnership firms, while the NCLT handles companies and LLPs.

s: Which of the following was NOT replaced by the National Company Law Tribunal?
x: The NCLT replaced the CLB, BIFR and AAIFR; it did not replace SAT.

s: To which body do appeals against orders of the NCLAT lie?
x: NCLAT (Delhi and Chennai) hears appeals from the NCLT, and its orders go on appeal to the Supreme Court.

s: Under which Act were Debt Recovery Tribunals set up?
o: Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993
x: DRTs were established under the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993; they are also used under SARFAESI.

s: Debt Recovery Tribunals deal with debts due to banks and financial institutions above what amount?
x: The DRTs and DRATs handle debts above ₹20 lakh under the stated framework.

s: Which mechanism accounted for the largest share of bank recoveries in FY 2024?
x: In FY 2024, IBC accounted for 48% of recoveries, SARFAESI 32%, DRTs 17% and Lok Adalats 3%.

s: From which Act do Lok Adalats, which help settle small non-performing assets, derive their statutory status?
o: The Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993
x: Lok Adalats are statutory forums under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

s: Which of the following allows secured lenders to recover dues without court intervention?
x: SARFAESI allows secured lenders to recover without courts; IBC is collective, NCLT-led resolution and DRTs are tribunal-based recovery.

s: To which body do appeals against orders of Debt Recovery Tribunals lie?
x: DRTs set up under the RDDBFI Act 1993 are backed by 5 Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunals (DRATs) for appeals.

s: India has 39 Debt Recovery Tribunals and how many Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunals?
x: There are 39 DRTs, with appeals going to 5 DRATs.

s: By what means do Lok Adalats mainly help settle small NPAs?
x: Lok Adalats, under the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987, settle small NPAs by compromise.

s: In which year was the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, under which Debt Recovery Tribunals were set up, passed?
x: DRTs were set up under the RDDBFI Act of 1993; Lok Adalats date from 1987, SARFAESI from 2002 and the IBC from 2016.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: ARCs — registered with RBI under SARFAESI
CDR — restructuring outside court for large multi-bank borrowers
Lok Adalats — conversion of lender debt into a 51 per cent equity stake
ARCs — purchase bad loans against security receipts
x: Conversion of lender debt into a 51 per cent or more equity stake is associated with Strategic Debt Restructuring, not Lok Adalats. ARCs, CDR and Lok Adalats have the other stated functions.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the SARFAESI Act, 2002?
o: Lenders holding 60% of the dues can issue a 60-day notice under Section 13(2)
The threshold was 75% of dues before the 2016 amendment
Under Section 13(4), lenders can take possession of the secured asset, take over management or sell it
Under Section 13(8), the borrower can redeem the asset after the auction notice by paying 25% of the dues
x: Under Section 13(8) the borrower can redeem only by paying the full dues, not 25%.

s: On the recommendations of which committee was the SARFAESI Act, 2002 based?
x: The SARFAESI Act, 2002 was based on the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee.

s: Within how many days does an appeal lie to the DRT under Section 17 of the SARFAESI Act?
x: Section 17 allows an appeal to the DRT within 45 days; the Section 13(2) demand notice is of 60 days.

s:
Consider the following about Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs):
1. They acquire NPAs, generally at a discount.
2. They are regulated by SEBI.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: ARCs acquire NPAs, generally at a discount, and are regulated by the RBI, not SEBI.

s: Under Section 13(8) of the SARFAESI Act, what must a borrower pay to redeem the secured asset?
x: Section 13(8) allows redemption only on payment of the full dues, not 25%.

s: Under Section 13(2) of the SARFAESI Act, lenders holding at least what share of the dues may issue a 60-day notice?
x: Section 13(2) lets lenders with 60% of the dues issue a 60-day notice to the borrower.

s: In which year was the SARFAESI Act, which lets secured lenders recover dues without going to court, enacted?
x: The SARFAESI Act was enacted in 2002 on the Narasimham Committee's ideas.

s: NARCL, described as India’s ‘bad bank’, was announced in which Budget?
x: The National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL) was announced in Budget 2021–22.

s: What share of the price of stressed assets does NARCL pay in cash, the rest being paid in Security Receipts?
x: NARCL pays 15% in cash and 85% in Security Receipts; the Government guarantee of Rs 30,600 crore runs for 5 years.

s: NARCL primarily targets stressed loans above which threshold and an aggregate asset value of approximately what amount?
x: NARCL takes over large stressed loans above ₹500 crore, targeting about ₹2 lakh crore of fully or partly provided assets.

s: What is the Government guarantee on security receipts issued by NARCL?
x: The Government guarantees NARCL's security receipts up to ₹30,600 crore for 5 years.

s: In India's bad bank structure, which entity resolves the stressed assets aggregated by NARCL?
x: NARCL aggregates the stressed loans; IDRCL (majority private) resolves them.

s:
Consider the following statements about NARCL and IDRCL:
1. Public sector banks hold a majority in NARCL.
2. IDRCL is majority privately owned.
3. NARCL resolves the assets, while IDRCL aggregates them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: PSBs hold a majority in NARCL and IDRCL is majority private; statement 3 reverses the roles: NARCL aggregates, IDRCL resolves.

s: To cases involving what amounts does the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 apply?
x: The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 covers offenders in cases involving ₹100 crore or more.

s: Under the RBI Master Direction of July 2024, wilful default must be examined in NPA accounts of what size?
x: The Master Direction of 30 July 2024 requires examination of wilful default in NPAs of ₹25 lakh and above.

s: Under the RBI Master Direction of July 2024, within what time must the classification of a wilful defaulter be completed?
x: The 2024 Master Direction requires classification within six months, and wilful defaulters get no restructuring.
